text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- Government plans to grant fiscal facilities to inhabitants of the Danube Delta, affected by plummeting living standards.
ADEVARUL
- Nuclear power plant at Cernavoda produced 2.8 percent of Romania's electricity in August.
- Some 6,000 workers at Prodex SA heavy equipment in Braila maker on pay strike.
- Romania loses ground in competition to enter European Union, the paper says.

- Project by U.S. Bell Helicopter Textron to build Cobra attack helicopters in Romania might boost U.S. investments in the country, Alfred Moses, United States ambassador to Romania says in interview.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Fuel crisis to come to an end next month when Romania plans to import some 600,000 tonnes of crude oil and 100,000 tonnes liquefied gas.
LIBERTATEA
- Romania's electricity consumption dropped by 30 percent over past six years following closure of some industrial units.
General:
All newspaper report on signing ceremony of long-delayed Romanian-Hungarian political treaty scheduled for September 16 in the western city of Timisoara.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Newspaper publishes programme launched by Emil Constantinescu, head of the opposition Democratic Convention CDR) and presidential candidate for the November 3 polls, on improving living standards of Romania's peasants.
- Opposition Social Democratic Union (USD) and National Liberal Alliance (ANL) signed agreement for the November 3 elections.
- Lower Chamber of Deputies resumed debates on penal code.
ADEVARUL

- Editorial on three major presidential candidates -- President Ion Iliescu, ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) candidate, USD candidate former reformist premier Petre Roman and CDR candidate Emil Constantinescu.
- It is important for Romania to have a center government says Alfred Moses, United States ambassador to Bucharest, in interview.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- One-page report on official start of electoral campaign for the November 3 general polls.
LIBERTATEA

- Meningitis epidemic, which broke out in Bucharest last month, might delay opening of school year on September 16, said Health Minister Daniela Bartos. ($=3,166 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
